presentation.label: MODULATED SPACE
presentation.summary: A modulated feedback-delay reverb after the Erbe-Verb: size, decay past 100 %, absorb, chorus, grains, shimmer, reverse and tilt.
presentation.overview: Four delay lines with diffusing allpasses, absorbing low-passes and a soft-saturating decay feed each other through a Hadamard matrix at 22.05 kHz. DPTH sweeps from a cyclic chorus through random ergodic grains into octave shimmer; REV plays the pre-delay backwards; EDCY and ESIZ route the reverb's own envelope into decay and size. The dry signal is never processed.
highlights: Size from a 2 ms box to a 143 ms hall, gliding without zipper noise
Decay up to 120 %: sustains and saturates above about 106
Cyclic, ergodic and shimmer modulation on one bipolar knob, with its speed beside it
Reverse pre-delay, tilt EQ and envelope-to-decay/size routings
MIX 0 is the exact dry signal
usage: Choose E-Verb in FX2 SETUP: hold FUNC, press FX2, turn LEVEL to the end of the list and press YES.
On the main page, MIX (encoder F) sets dry/wet; SIZE, DCY and ABSB shape the space; DPTH left is chorus, right is grains, the last sixteen steps are shimmer; SPD sets how fast it moves.
On the SETUP page, TILT darkens or brightens the wet, PRE sets the pre-delay, REV reverses it, and EDCY/ESIZ send the reverb's envelope into DCY and SIZE.
The six main-page knobs take parameter locks, LFOs, scenes and MIDI CC like any stock effect's; the SETUP knobs are set per Part.

controls.name: SIZE
controls.doc: Scales every delay and allpass over six octaves: the longest line runs 2.2 ms at 0, 18 ms at 64 and 143 ms at 127. Moving it glides the pitch of the tail, smoothed per frame.

controls.name: DCY
controls.doc: Reflection gain from 0 to 120 %. Below about 106 the tail decays (short at 40, minutes at 100 with large sizes); above, it sustains and the in-loop saturation holds the level.

controls.name: ABSB
controls.doc: 0..38 adds diffusion (allpass gain up to 0.8); 38..127 adds damping inside the loop, darker and shorter.

controls.name: DPTH
controls.doc: Bipolar modulation, 0 at the centre. Left: cyclic chorus/doppler. Right: ergodic grains to +47; from +48 a growing share of grains glides up an octave (shimmer), about half at +56.

controls.name: SPD
controls.doc: Modulation speed 0.5 Hz to 256 Hz (about 12 Hz at 64): the cyclic rate or the grain rate; in the shimmer zone SIZE sets the grain length.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: Equal-power dry/wet. 0 is exactly the dry input; 127 is all reverb.

controls.name: TILT
controls.doc: SETUP A. Bipolar wet tone. Left: lows below 250 Hz up to +12 dB, highs down (about -14 dB at 9 kHz). Right: highs above 2 kHz up to +24 dB, lows down 3 to 5 dB. Centre is flat. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: PRE
controls.doc: SETUP B. Pre-delay 7 ms at 0, 42 ms at 64, 250 ms at 127; with REV on, the reverse window (at least 42 ms). Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: REV
controls.doc: SETUP C. Plays the pre-delay buffer backwards in crossfaded windows; a change ducks, switches in silence and reopens without a click. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: EDCY
controls.doc: SETUP D. Bipolar: the reverb's envelope into DCY. Left reins the tail in when loud; right rings longer when loud, up to the decay of DCY 95, never into sustain (no effect from DCY 96 up). Centre is off. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: ESIZ
controls.doc: SETUP E. Bipolar: the reverb's envelope into SIZE. Left shrinks the space when loud; right grows it. Centre is off. Not lockable (SETUP page).

limitations: Owner reports working sound on MKII plus two distinct simultaneous T1/T5 instances, Part/project save and reload, and physical reboot on EVRB01T01. MKI, maximum-load silicon timing and broader hardware modulation/recovery tests remain unverified.
FX2 only: the effect needs the 16K-word delay buffer the OS gives FX2 instances.

With stock DSP code built in, E-Verb's 1,588 words take the space of two FX2-only stock reverbs. On its own it gives up SPRING REV and DARK REV: they leave the FX2 chooser, and a saved project that uses either on FX2 plays that slot dry. PLATE REV and every other stock effect stay. Other modules in the same build can change the choice.
The SETUP page (TILT, PRE, REV, EDCY, ESIZ) is not lockable: the OS keeps parameter locks, LFO, scene and CC targets for the six main-page knobs of an FX slot only.

Dearer than any stock effect: up to 376 executed instructions per sample without trig splits (SPRING REV 258, DJ EQ 293) and 382 with them (SPRING REV 314, DJ EQ 331). Four per core fit the static budget; real-chip headroom beside heavy FX1 effects is not measured.
A sustained full-scale tone on a room resonance can clip at high MIX, and TILT far right or a sustaining DCY can clip the wet at the tank rate; DCY above about 106 sustains and saturates by design.
No tempo sync: as on the hardware and the stock reverbs, SPD is in Hz and PRE in milliseconds.

storage.label: DSP program / buffer
storage.conditions: 1,588 assembled program words on each DSP core, placed in the space of SPRING REV and DARK REV with 449 words to spare before PLATE REV's helper; a 132-word X state block per instance; 16,369 of the 16,384 Y words the OS already allocates to every FX2 instance.

processing.label: DSP instruction peak
processing.conditions: benchmark_stock_dsp.py's method (one instance per core, 16-sample blocks, null stub subtracted) with the stock effects run through the same cases: worst case at the dearest settings with a trig split, 381.7 (375.8 unsplit). Static loop count 468 cycles/sample. Executed instructions, not chip cycles.

impact.conditions: One active instance at its dearest settings (SIZE 0, DPTH 127, REV on) with moving controls and trig splits; the 16K buffer is the stock FX2 allocation, reused.

cpu.rationale: No ColdFire code: the stock parameter pages publish the knobs, as for any FX2 effect.

dsp.rationale: 381.7 executed instructions/sample worst case with trig splits, against 314.2 for SPRING REV and 330.9 for DJ EQ (the dearest stock effect) under the same cases; the full-call software bound for four per core is 47,680 of 49,920 modeled cycles per 16-frame block. Chip timing is unmeasured.

memory.rationale: 1,588 program words per core in two given-up stock reverbs' space, a 132-word X block per instance, and the 16K-word FX2 delay buffer every reverb already gets.

tests.summary: Render gates pass on a native image: exact dry at MIX 0, pre-delay/decay/stereo laws, eight-instance isolation under guard and dirty start, garbage start, no zipper on any continuous knob, trig splits, REV switching, DPTH locked between shimmer and chorus, and EDCY unable to hold a tail. Static 468 cycles/sample, 381.7 instructions/sample measured against stock under the same cases; 32 s stress with eight instances, LFOs, locks and splits: no clobber, no hang. Owner reports a positive MKII functional audition on the exact EVRB01T01 image; detailed hardware coverage remains limited.
gates: verify.py: source and init rules, static cycles, native placement, exact dry, reverb laws, idle, eight-instance isolation (-guard -dirty), garbage start, zipper census, trig splits, REV switching, DPTH locks, EDCY latch
evidence/performance.json: perf:audit (static, stock benchmark under matched cases, 32 s stress)
npm run fx:audit at the dearest settings, the defaults and each modulation mode
Hardware: owner-reported MKII functional audition on EVRB01T01; detailed coverage in evidence/owner-hardware.md.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Select an audio track, hold FUNC and press FX2, turn LEVEL to E-Verb at the end of the list and press YES.
Press FX2 to open the main page, turn encoder F (MIX) to 100 and play a sample: the reverb follows each hit. Turn encoder D (DPTH) to +56 for grains with a rising octave shimmer.
Turn MIX back to 0 to hear the exact dry signal, or set FX2 back to DELAY or NONE in FX2 SETUP to remove the effect.

conditions.parameterExtremes: Conservative assembled-word bound, both alternating sample arms, all 24 knob helper call sites and both fixed-length clearing loops; every branch and parameter endpoint is included even when mutually exclusive.
conditions.parameterModulation: Two calls per 16-frame block cover trigger splits; all knob groups and helper visits are charged on each call. LFO, locks, scenes and CC reach the same knob publication path. No contention or silicon wall-clock timing is claimed.
conditions.modeSwitching: Both init and ring warm-up clear bounds are charged twice per block, in addition to all prologue/group words. REV and depth branches use the worst union bound. Part/project/reboot behavior is separately reported hardware evidence.
conditions.maxLoad: Eight FX2 instances, four per DSP core, at 44.1 kHz and 16 frames per block. Per-core bound 47,680 within the SDK 49,920 module allowance; stock/scheduling reserve remains separate. Arbitrary companion load and real-chip contention are unmeasured.
conditions.inputConditions: Word-span bound does not depend on sample magnitude; both audio-rate branches, saturation, feedback, silence, impulses and full-scale inputs are covered. Source/render measurements are in TESTING.md.

regions.name: Used and initialized stock X state, r7+0..0x83
Reserved remainder of 256-word stock X block
Reserved stock FX2 Y ring, 16,369 words used
Dispatcher and one do/bsr stack on both cores

memory.conditions: Reserved 256-word X block and 16,384-word Y ring per FX2 instance, including unused padding; code shared once per core. No authored heap, SDRAM arena, ColdFire executable or callback. Existing stock dispatcher stack is bounded to a call plus one nonnested do/bsr on each core. Logical 24-bit DSP words; flash descriptors use byte accounting. Guarded eight-instance software evidence does not claim hardware canaries.

hardware.summary: Owner reports a positive MKII audition (“super sick”) on EVRB01T01 and explicitly confirms all requested T1/T5 simultaneous-instance, Part/project save/reload and physical reboot checks passed.
limitations: These are attributed owner-reported functional results; the agent did not observe the physical unit and no detailed stress qualification is claimed.
Duration, maximum eight-instance hardware load, MIDI/USB load, every control/modulation endpoint, recovery and hardware canaries are not reported.
Cycle values are software bounds; whole-chip contention and wall-clock timing are not measured.
